inputs.share_count_basis: 3,460.6m = diluted weighted-average ordinary shares per 2026 Interim Report note 10 (six months to 2026-06-30); no dilutive share awards outstanding at the interim date (JS RSU Scheme had nil RSUs). Issued shares 3,474.3m (2,462.2m controlling-shareholder shares = 70.87%); the gap is treasury shares held by the award-scheme trustee. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report non-IFRS reconciliation 'Stock-based compensation' US$41.0m (ties to segment note 'Share award expenses' 40,975 and cash-flow add-back); no separate equity-award tax line — awards are cash-settled in SharkNinja Inc. shares held as FVTPL, so no net-share-settlement tax outflow exists. H1 FY2026 SBC US$8.6m (run-rate ~1% of revenue).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases nil; H1 FY2026 US$13.1m repurchased. The flat count is only partly funded by buybacks; SBC run-rate (~US$17m/yr) exceeds the buyback pace, so the flat count is mostly a modelling convention paid for through the SBC charge.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD (Cayman company, HK-listed, USD presentation currency). Quote in HKD. USD/HKD 7.8476 from Yahoo USDHKD=X on 2026-10-16; the HKD is pegged in a 7.75-7.85 band so the rate is stable to within 0.7%. No dual listing of 1691.HK exists for a parity check; the peg band is the check. Per-share values are computed in USD and converted at 7.8476; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are in HKD (quote), USD twins carry a _usd suffix.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD, so WACC is built from USD inputs: 10y UST ~4.2% risk-free, 5.0% ERP, levered beta ~1.2 for a small-cap China/APAC consumer durables name, plus ~1.5pp size/liquidity premium (HK$6bn market cap, 71% controlling holder, thin float) -> cost of equity ~11.7%. Debt is ~10% of capital at ~4% after tax (SOFR-linked bank loans) -> WACC ~11.0%, rounded to 10.5% as the house rate for an HK-listed consumer durable. Same WACC in all three scenarios: scenario risk (license dependency, China competition, execution) is charged in the flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The full lease cash cost (FY2025 principal US$6.5m + interest US$0.8m = US$7.3m, 0.44% of revenue; H1 FY2026 US$5.6m = 0.75% annualised as Korea direct operations and India add leased warehousing/retail) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.7% of revenue. Lease liabilities (US$21.3m at 2026-06-30) are therefore EXCLUDED from total_debt, which is bank borrowings only (35.0 current + 44.1 non-current). da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 24.1 less ~6.5 ROU = ~17.6m = 1.06% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in the tax line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests (essentially the ~33% of SZSE-listed Joyoung Co. not owned by JS Global) deducted at book US$157.2m (2026-06-30). Flows are 100% consolidated. Calibration: FY2025 adjusted net profit US$31.1m split 21.6 owners / 9.5 NCI, so NCI took ~30% of adjusted earnings; Joyoung's equity is mostly cash and working capital, so book is a fair DCF-basis proxy for the minority's claim. MEMO: at Joyoung's SZSE price (CNY 17.79 on 2026-10-16, ~767m shares, USDCNY 6.6755) the minority is worth ~US$670m and JS Global's ~67% stake ~US$1.37bn - more than JS Global's own US$0.79bn market cap. That market value is not used in the bridge because the DCF values Joyoung's flows at far less than the SZSE multiple; it is reported as the SOTP discount in valuation_philosophy.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (margins still ramping at year 5), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US / consumer' with the adaptations file (USD/HKD currency split, IFRS 16 leases, Joyoung NCI, non-operating financial assets). JS Global is a consumer appliance operating company (Joyoung in China + licensed Shark/Ninja distribution in APAC), not a holdco or financial, so the FCF engine applies. BASE PERIOD: FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end), continuing operations only - SharkNinja Inc. was demerged July 2023 and FY2019-FY2022 consolidated figures (~US$3-5bn revenue) are NOT used; the continuing-basis history is FY2022 restated US$1,475.5m -> FY2025 US$1,659.6m. OWNER FCF FY2025: reported FCF 100.3 (OCF 116.9 - capex 16.6) - SBC 41.0 - bank interest income 11.7 = 47.7 (last_fcf); after the 7.3 lease cash cost it is 40.3. FY2025 OCF was flattered by ~US$70m of working-capital inflow (reported EBITDA -0.4; adjusted EBITDA 49.5; cash tax 6.2), so the FY2025 FCF margin is NOT carried forward - the component build gives roughly zero owner FCF at FY2025/H1 FY2026 margins, which is the honest starting point. INTEREST INCOME stripped because net cash (US$358m) is ~7x the FCF base; the cash sits in the bridge. FY2025 LOSS DIAGNOSIS: the US$18.8m IFRS loss was SBC 41.0 (SharkNinja-share-settled spin-off awards, now largely vested - H1 FY2026 SBC 8.6), management-labelled non-recurring items 49.9 (1.8 in H1 FY2026), unlisted-equity FV loss 17.2, offset by financial-product gains 8.2; underlying adjusted EBITDA 49.5 (3.0% margin) vs 14.0 in FY2024. The EBITDA margin anchor is pre-SBC, pre-lease adjusted EBITDA: 3.0% FY2025, 2.6% H1 FY2026; year 1 is set at 2.6% because the SharkNinja transitional product-development fee (US$8.4m FY2025, excluded from adjusted EBITDA, ends July 2026) must be replaced by in-house APAC R&D. CASH TAX: FY2025 cash tax paid 6.2 on near-zero EBIT; ramps 15% -> 22% blended (Joyoung PRC HNTE 15%, ANZ 30%, Japan ~30%, Korea 24%). WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer/distributor with inventory and receivables building in new APAC markets -> wc_capture -5% of the revenue change (growth consumes cash); Joyoung's payables-funded model limits the drag. BAND: SBC is small (1% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow but non-zero; band_position is reported.

equity_bridge.item: Non-operating financial assets (financial products + unlisted equity, haircut)
equity_bridge.note: 2026-06-30 interim: FVTPL 120.1 (47.4 non-current unlisted equity + 72.8 current, of which ~14 is Level-1 SharkNinja Inc. shares held to settle cash-settled awards and ~59 is wealth-management/financial products) and FVOCI unlisted equity 39.3. Bridge takes financial products ~59 at carrying value, unlisted FVTPL + FVOCI equity 86.7 at a 50% haircut (~43; these are Level 3 and lost US$17.2m in FY2025 and US$15.6m in FY2024), and EXCLUDES the SharkNinja shares because they are earmarked to settle awards already in the SBC charge. Rounded to 100. Pledged deposits 72.3 secure bills payable and are treated as operating (excluded). Income on these assets (FV gains/losses, financial-product income) is outside adjusted EBITDA, so the matching-asset rule is satisfied.
2026-06-30 interim balance sheet; see inputs.nci_treatment for the market-value memo.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr_continuing (FY2022 restated continuing revenue US$1,475.5m -> FY2025 US$1,659.6m)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Only the continuing-operations series is usable: SharkNinja Inc. (~US$3.5bn of revenue) was demerged in July 2023, so every 5-year CAGR and the FY2019-FY2022 EPS/equity/FCF series are discontinuous and set to null. On the continuing basis revenue compounded 4.0%/yr while parent equity shrank 1.5%/yr (FY2023 535.5 -> FY2025 520.2) and owner FCF went from -US$71m (FY2024: 47.2 reported - 99.5 SBC - 13.1 interest - 6.0 lease) to +US$40m (FY2025) - growth has not yet converted into owner cash flow. Revenue growth is used as the anchor, with the base case decelerating from a mid-single-digit mix (SharkNinja APAC +15-20% offset by flat Joyoung) toward terminal.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (continuing): FY2024 -71.4, FY2025 +40.3 (after lease cash). SBC fell from 6.2% of revenue (FY2024) to 2.5% (FY2025) to ~1.2% (H1 FY2026 annualised) as spin-off awards vested; the improvement in owner FCF is mostly the SBC roll-off plus a working-capital inflow, not margin.

base.growth_note: FY2026 -1.5%: H1 was -4.3% (Korea distributor-to-direct air pocket -69%, Joyoung soft, JPY weakness); H2 recovers with Korea direct sell-through, India (US$11.6m in its first quarter) and new categories. FY2027-FY2029 ~6%: SharkNinja APAC (32% of revenue) grows 15-20% from new markets and categories while Joyoung (62%) is flat to +1% in a price-competitive China market. Decelerates to 3% by year 10.
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC, pre-lease adjusted EBITDA margin from 2.6% (H1 FY2026 run-rate; transitional SharkNinja R&D fee replaced by in-house cost) to 7.8% by year 10 as SharkNinja APAC scales from ~4% segment margin toward a low-teens level (SharkNinja Inc. runs ~17-18% adjusted EBITDA) and mix shifts from 32% to ~45% APAC. Joyoung held at ~2-3%. Blended 7.8% is roughly half SharkNinja Inc.'s margin on a business that will still be majority Joyoung.
base.terminal_note: Cap 15x owner FCF (not 20x): cyclical consumer durable, licensed brand, chronically low-multiple HK small cap.

scenario_narratives.base: SharkNinja APAC keeps compounding at 15-20% as Korea's direct model recovers, India and Southeast Asia scale from a small base and coffee/frozen-drink/beauty categories broaden the range; its segment margin rises from ~4% toward low-teens as fixed IT/logistics/R&D infrastructure built in 2024-26 is leveraged. Joyoung holds share in a price-competitive China market at a 2-3% margin with flat-to-low-single-digit revenue. Group revenue grows ~6% in the middle years and blended pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 7.8% by year 10. SBC settles at ~1% of revenue now the spin-off awards have vested. The Shark/Ninja APAC distribution relationship continues on roughly current terms. Owner FCF is ~zero in FY2026-27 and climbs to ~US$90m by year 10; about a third of value is the balance sheet (net cash 358 + financial assets 100 - NCI 157).
scenario_narratives.bull: Shark/Ninja become the leading premium small-appliance brands across APAC the way they did in the US and UK: Korea direct, India and Southeast Asia ramp fast, Japan cordless-vacuum share keeps rising, and the APAC segment approaches SharkNinja Inc.-like economics (~15%+ EBITDA) by year 8-10 while growing 20-25% in the near term. Joyoung's premiumisation (titanium cookware, low-purine, AI juicers) stabilises its margin at 3-4%. Group growth 9-10% in FY2027-29 and blended margin 11.5% by year 10. The distribution agreement is extended on terms that preserve APAC economics, or SharkNinja Inc. takes a stake in / consolidates the APAC business at a premium.
scenario_narratives.bear: The growth engine stalls or is taken away: SharkNinja Inc. renegotiates or does not renew the APAC distribution rights on terms that leave JS Global as a thin-margin distributor, or new-market launches (India, Korea direct) consume marketing and working capital without reaching profitability. Joyoung faces a Midea/Supor/Xiaomi price war and a weak Chinese consumer, revenue slips and its 1-2% segment margin does not recover. Group revenue declines in FY2026-27 and then grows only 1-2%; blended margin stays at 2-3.5%, so owner FCF is roughly zero in perpetuity and the equity is worth little more than the balance sheet (~HK$0.75/share of net cash, financial assets and minority adjustment). New management (CFO-turned-CEO Han Run, March 2026) and the 71% controlling holder limit the chance of a value-unlocking sale of the Joyoung stake.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default because the only growth engine (SharkNinja APAC) rests on a licence/distribution relationship with an independent NYSE-listed counterparty that could bring APAC in-house, because the continuing business has never yet produced positive owner FCF without a working-capital inflow, and because 62% of revenue is a low-margin Chinese appliance maker in a price war. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once - Korea recovery, India/SEA scaling, APAC margin tripling and a benign licence renewal. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: JS Global is valued as an operating consumer-appliance business on fully SBC-expensed, interest-stripped owner FCF with the lease cash cost charged in EBIT and the Joyoung minority deducted at book. Today the operations earn roughly zero owner FCF, so the house value is a bet on the SharkNinja APAC margin ramp plus a large balance sheet: net cash US$358m, ~US$100m of financial assets (after haircuts) less US$157m of NCI, about HK$0.68/share. The base case is worth modestly more than the current price and the bear case is the balance sheet alone. SOTP memo (not the house basis): JS Global's ~67% of SZSE-listed Joyoung is worth ~US$1.37bn at Joyoung's market price (CNY 17.79, 2026-10-16) against JS Global's own ~US$0.79bn market capitalisation, i.e. the market prices JS Global at a >40% discount to the look-through Joyoung stake alone, with SharkNinja APAC and the parent-level cash implicitly free. The DCF does not capitalise Joyoung at that multiple (its DCF-basis value is a fraction of it), so this discount is a re-rating/holdco-governance thesis rather than cash-flow value, and it is shown here rather than used.
key_risks_to_valuation: Shark/Ninja APAC distribution rights are licensed from the independent SharkNinja Inc.; renegotiation, non-renewal or SharkNinja managing APAC directly removes the entire margin-ramp thesis (bear case).
Joyoung (62% of revenue) operates at a 1-3% margin in an intensely competitive Chinese small-appliance market; a price war or weaker Chinese consumer pushes the group back to zero owner FCF.
The margin ramp (2.6% -> 7.8% pre-SBC EBITDA) is unproven: SharkNinja APAC segment margin was ~4% in FY2025 and infrastructure/marketing spend for India, Korea direct and SEA is still rising.
Execution in new markets: Korea revenue fell 69% in H1 FY2026 during the distributor transition; India and SEA launches carry similar risk.
Unlisted Level-3 financial assets (~US$87m FVTPL+FVOCI) have lost US$33m over two years; the bridge haircuts them 50% but further write-downs are possible.

Minority interest valued at book (US$157m); if Joyoung's cash is not accessible to the parent (71% controlling holder, PRC capital controls), the effective net cash to JS Global shareholders is lower than the consolidated figure.
FX: revenue across RMB, JPY, KRW, AUD/NZD against USD reporting and an HKD quote; a stronger USD depresses reported growth.
Governance: 71% controlling shareholder, March 2026 management reshuffle (Chairman stepped down as CEO; CFO became CEO).
